q: In the pronunciation line BAH-tahq (bata, child), what does the q stand for?
o: A catch: the breath stops at the end
A k sound at the end
why: q marks a catch at the end of the word: stop the breath, and add no k.

q: How many syllables does maayo (good) have?
o: Three: ma-a-yo, with a catch before the second a
why: Two vowels side by side are two syllables, with a catch between them.

q: How do you say mga, the plural word?
why: mga is written short but said manga.

q: It is 3 p.m. and you meet a neighbor. What do you say?
why: From early afternoon until dark the greeting is Maayong hapon.

q: A jeepney driver hands you your change. What is the most polite thanks?
why: An older man or a driver is Nong; po is Tagalog, and Nang is for a woman.

q: Someone says Salamat. You answer:
why: Walay sapayan means you're welcome.

q: How do you say Just one?
why: lang never comes first: it follows the main word, Usa lang.

q: Someone says Maayong buntag! How do you say Good morning to you too?
why: sab means too, and it goes after the greeting.

q: What does diay add to a sentence?
o: It turns it into a yes-or-no question
Surprise: you have just learned it
why: diay shows you have just found something out: oh, so it is.

q: The vendor is holding a fruit you don't know. How do you ask What's that?
why: A thing near the listener is kana, and the question word comes first.

q: How do you say This is a book?
why: The main word comes first and there is no word for is: Libro kini.

q: In Unsa ni?, what is ni?
why: After another word, kini is often shortened to ni.

q: How do you say I'm American (a man)?
why: The main word comes first, then the short form ko.

q: Which marker goes before a person's name, as in Maestra ___ Ana?
why: Names take si; other nouns take ang.

q: What does siya mean?
why: siya is both he and she.

q: How do you ask a new friend where they are from?
why: taga- + asa asks where someone is from; Asa ka gikan? asks where they have just been.

q: How do you say I'm Emma?
why: Start with the full form ako; names take si.

q: What does imong mean in Unsay imong ngalan?
why: imong is your; it goes before the noun, like akong.

q: How do you ask Where are you going?
why: The question word comes first, then the short form ka.

q: Which word means who?
why: kinsa is who; unsa is what, asa is where, ngano is why.

q: How do you say No (to a yes-or-no question like Amerikano ka ba?)
why: Dili is Cebuano no; hindi is Tagalog, and oo is yes.

q: You tell a vendor We're from the US (you and your wife). Which do you say?
why: The vendor is not included, so the we is kami, short form mi.

q: kamo means:
why: kamo is you for two or more people.

q: How do you make bata (child) plural?
why: Put mga before the noun; Cebuano never adds -s.

q: Pedro's house =
why: Names take ni when they own something.

q: our house (yours and mine) =
why: atong includes the listener; among and namo leave them out.

q: the door of the house =
why: An owner that is not a name takes sa.

q: a big house =
why: The linker joins the two words: dako + -ng, dakong balay.

q: What does Dako ang balay mean?
why: With the describing word first and ang before the noun, it is a full sentence.

q: very good =
why: kaayo after the describing word means very; lang, ba and diay mean other things.

q: How do you say "I have water"?
why: naa + ko + -y: literally "there is, mine, some water".

q: What does Walay kape mean?
why: walay is wala + -y: there is no.

q: Which sentence asks whether Ana is there?
why: Names take si, and naa without -y says where someone is.

q: How do you say "I'm thirsty"?
why: The feeling comes first, then the short pronoun ko.

q: Where does kaayo (very) usually go?
o: After the feeling word: Kapoy kaayo.
Before the feeling word: Kaayo kapoy.
At the very start, before everything else
It is never used with feelings
why: kaayo follows the word it makes stronger.

q: What does Masakit akong ulo mean?
why: masakit = hurts; akong ulo = my head.

q: How do you say "three bananas"?
why: A Cebuano number needs ka before the noun.

q: Which numbers are used for prices?
why: Prices are said in Spanish numbers (English is heard too, but never only English).

q: How do you say "I have two children"?
why: The number comes first, and akong (with -ng) goes before the noun.

q: What does Tagpila? ask?
o: The price of each piece or kilo
why: tag- means each, per: Tagpila? = how much each?

q: A kilo costs ₱40. The vendor says:
why: The price first, in Spanish numbers, then ang and the thing.

q: Where do you ask Pwede pahangyo?
why: Asking for a small discount is normal at a market, not where prices are fixed.

q: What does igsoon mean?
why: igsoon says nothing about sex: add nga lalaki or nga babaye.

q: Pedro is Ana's husband. Which is right?
why: ni before the owner's name, si before the name of the person you talk about.

q: Talking to a guest, how do you say "our family"?
why: among leaves the listener out; atong would include the guest.

q: How do you say "I ate yesterday"?
why: It already happened, so ni-; ko follows the verb.

q: What does mo- show?
o: The action has not happened yet, or is a habit
The action was done to you
why: mo- is the future form, also used for habits.

q: How do you say "I'll buy water"?
why: mo- for the future, ko right after the verb, og before the water.

q: What can Nagluto siya mean?
o: She cooked, or she is cooking.
why: nag- covers something done and something going on now.

q: How do you say "I'll study"?
why: mag- is the future form, and ko follows the verb.

q: What does Magdula ta! mean?
why: mag- with ta (we, including you) is a suggestion: let's.

q: How do you say "I didn't go"?
why: wala for the past, ko right after it, and the verb in the mo- form.

q: Which word is right in ___ ko Amerikano (I'm not American)?
why: No verb and no 'there is': the 'not' is dili.

q: After wala, which form does the verb take?
why: wala already says it did not happen, so this course keeps the verb in the mo- form.

q: How do you say "three o'clock"?
why: On the clock: alas + a Spanish number.

q: What does unya mean?
why: unya is later today; tomorrow is ugma.

q: Which one is "seven p.m."?
why: alas + Spanish siyete, and sa gabii for the evening.

q: How do you say 'I want to eat'?
why: No word for 'to': gusto ko, then the verb with mo-.

q: Which sentence means 'I need help'?
why: kinahanglan comes first, ko right after it, then og and the thing.

q: A child reaches for a hot pan. Which word means 'Don't!'?
why: ayaw tells someone not to do something; dili and wala describe.

q: You want a jeepney driver (an older man) to wait a moment. Which is most polite?
why: lang softens the command and Nong shows respect; Cebuano has no po.

q: What does 'Palihug ko og tubig' mean?
why: Palihug ko og… is the everyday way to ask for something: 'please me some…'.

q: Which word begins 'Don't worry': '__ kabalaka'?
why: ayaw tells someone not to do something: Ayaw kabalaka.

q: How do you order one soup?
why: A Cebuano number joins the food with ka: usa ka sabaw.

q: What is kan-on?
why: kan-on is cooked rice; uncooked rice is bugas.

q: Your host offers more food and you've had enough. You say:
why: Busog na ko: 'I'm full (already)'.

q: Which word means 'there', near the person you're talking to?
why: diha is near you, like kana; didto is far from you both.

q: Which sentence means 'I'm going to the market'?
why: sa covers 'to', and ko stays right after the verb.

q: diri and dinhi both mean…
why: diri and dinhi are two words for 'here'.

q: What does 'Lugar lang' tell the driver?
why: Lugar lang means 'just here': you want to get off.

q: Which means 'Turn left'?
why: Left is wala, right is tuo.

q: Why must you say Para! out loud on a jeepney?
o: It is how you pay the fare
Jeepneys have no fixed stops, so the driver stops only when asked
It is the greeting for the driver
why: No fixed stops: the driver waits for Para! or Lugar lang.

q: What does 'Paliton nako ang saging' mean?
why: -on is the future form of a thing-focus verb.

q: Why is 'Gipalit ako ang saging' wrong?
o: The doer of a gi- verb takes the nako-set: nako
why: With a thing-focus verb the doer takes the nako-set.

q: Which sentence means 'I'll buy some bananas' (any bananas)?
why: 'Some' bananas, with og, go with a doer-focus mo- verb.

q: Which sentence means 'I washed the plate'?
why: Past place-focus: gi-…-an, with the doer in the nako-set.

q: In 'Gitabangan nako si Pedro', why does Pedro have si?
o: He is the one who helps
He is the focus of a place-focus verb, and names take si
why: The person helped is the focus; a name that is the focus takes si.

q: How do you ask someone to wash the plate?
why: palihug plus the -i form asks someone to do something to a thing or person.

q: How do you say 'bigger'?
why: Cebuano puts mas before the describing word and never adds an ending.

q: Which word means 'than'?
why: kaysa means 'than': mas dako kaysa niana.

q: What does 'Pinakamahal ang litson' mean?
o: The lechon is the most expensive.
The lechon is the same price.
why: pinaka- means 'the most'.

q: What does 'Dili ko makaadto' mean?
why: dili + maka- is 'can't'; wala + maka- is 'couldn't'.

q: Which asks 'Have you ever been to Bohol?'
why: naka- with na asks whether something has ever happened.

q: You learned to cook as a child. Which says 'I know how to cook'?
why: kahibalo is 'know how' for a skill.
